about: Every feature of malves and how far it has been proven. CI runs `node scripts/check-features.mjs`: a feature needs evidence files that exist, and anything not yet proven on a real device must say how to prove it. Statuses: verified-real (seen working on a real phone, computer or service), automated-only (tests pass, not yet seen on a real device), awaiting-real-test (built, the owner still has to try it), known-issue (broken in a known way).

features.name: Every human decision goes through one place; silence stops the task
features.notes: Tested on a real phone with the demo agent and Claude (build steps 1 and 2).

features.name: Append-only event log; a phone resumes from where it left off
Encrypted phone link with a challenge handshake
Pair a phone by scanning a QR code
Pair from a malves://pair link (the phone's camera opens the app)
features.real_test: On the computer type `pair link`, scan the QR with the phone's camera app, tap Pair in the dialog, and check the phone ends up paired.

features.name: Run Claude Code through ACP
Run Codex through ACP
features.real_test: Start a small task with Codex from the phone and answer its permission question.

features.name: Run Antigravity (API key, never a Google login)
features.notes: Works, but takes about 30 seconds to start; shown as slow, not broken.

features.name: Run Cursor through its CLI
features.notes: The CLI installs as agent.cmd, which malves will not start through a shell; malves has to learn the real program behind it.
features.real_test: After the fix, start a small task with Cursor from the phone and answer its question.

features.name: Notifications through the ntfy app, with answer buttons
features.real_test: Lock the phone, start a task that asks permission, and answer it from the notification's buttons.

features.name: A phone that was away gets the notifications it missed
features.real_test: Turn the phone's data off, finish a task, turn it back on, and check the ntfy app shows that the task finished.

features.name: A waiting question is nudged twice before it times out
features.real_test: Start a task that asks a question, leave it unanswered, and check the phone is nudged again (the notification is replaced, not stacked).

features.name: malves doctor and the phone's Check setup page
features.real_test: Run `pnpm malves doctor`, then open Settings > Check setup on the phone and tap Check again.

features.name: Tokens and keys are written atomically and owner-only
features.real_test: On Linux or macOS check `ls -l ~/.malves/*.json` shows -rw------- for every secret file.

features.name: Secrets are hidden in serve.log and the vault conversation log
features.real_test: Start serve in the background, trigger an error that prints a key, and check serve.log shows [hidden].

features.name: Typed text never carries control or invisible characters
features.real_test: In handover mode ask Malves to type text containing a hidden character and check the read-back mentions it.

features.name: A log of who watched or controlled the computer
features.real_test: Watch and tap the screen from the phone, then run `pnpm malves audit` and check both appear once.

features.name: Watch the computer's screen as pictures
Watch the computer's screen as live video (WebRTC)
features.real_test: Open Your screen right after restarting serve and again later: live video should appear within a few seconds and move smoothly (the computer-side test measures about 14 frames a second at 1080p).

features.name: Click, scroll and type on the computer from the phone
features.real_test: Open Your screen, tap a button on the computer, scroll, and type a sentence into Notepad.

features.name: Handover mode: Malves keeps the computer until Stop, I'm back, or four hours
features.real_test: Say 'I'm leaving, take over', ask it to run the tests, and check risky commands are read back for your yes.

features.name: Malves, the assistant: tool calls proposed by the brain, decided by code
features.real_test: From the phone say 'start Claude on a small task', check it is read back, confirm it, and check the task starts.

features.name: Natural voice: Cartesia, then ElevenLabs, then Piper, then the phone's
Voice commands, hands-free mode and the floating mic
features.real_test: In the APK say 'what's running?' from Home and from another screen, and talk over a reply to stop it.

features.name: Malves rings the phone with Android's call screen (Firebase)
features.real_test: Settings > Calls > Test call, with the phone locked, and answer it.

features.name: Memory as Markdown notes in an Obsidian vault
features.notes: Runner side tested live; the phone's Memory page awaits a real test.

features.name: Nightly encrypted vault backup to your own server
features.notes: A round trip (backup then restore) was tested live.

features.name: A Markdown journal of finished tasks, with a weekly roll-up
features.real_test: Set MALVES_VAULT, finish a task, and open Journal/<today>.md in Obsidian.

features.name: Work profile that is kept true, edited only on your yes
features.real_test: Do something that contradicts About me.md and check Malves drafts a change and waits for your yes.

features.name: Advice drawn from the skills in ~/.claude/skills
features.real_test: Ask Malves a question one of your skills covers and check the reply names the skill.

features.name: One list of sessions across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Antigravity
features.real_test: Open Work > Sessions, read an earlier Claude session, and continue it from the phone.

features.name: Browser tasks through the Chrome extension
features.real_test: Load the extension, ask Malves to open a page and read it, and check a click asks your phone first.

features.name: One extension for VS Code, Cursor, Antigravity and Windsurf
features.real_test: From the phone, open a finished task's changes in VS Code on the computer.

features.name: Leads from signalstack on the phone, with a weekly digest
features.real_test: Run signalstack with real data, open the Leads tab, and check Monday's digest arrives.

features.name: Claude and Codex on free models with a quality floor
features.real_test: Run 'Claude (free models)' against a real freellmapi and check the phone shows the model that answered.

features.name: Review a finished task's changes and commit them from the phone
features.real_test: Finish a task that edits a file, open its changes on the phone, and approve the commit.

features.name: Reach the computer through your own relay (no Tailscale)
features.real_test: Run the relay on a server, start serve with --relay, and pair a phone on mobile data.

features.name: Start malves in the background when you log in to Windows
Every merge to main builds the APK, Chrome zip and VSIX and publishes a release
features.real_test: Merge a pull request and check a new release appears on the Releases page with all three files.

features.name: Install the computer side on Windows with no Node.js, pnpm or git
features.real_test: On a Windows PC with no Node.js, run install.ps1 from a release, then `malves doctor` and `malves serve`.

features.name: If Tailscale comes up after malves, serve restarts itself and binds to it
features.real_test: Turn Tailscale off, restart serve, wait two minutes, turn Tailscale on, and check serve restarts and the phone connects without you doing anything.
